start.title: Run Shell + MFE.
start.lead: Start a host application, add its microfrontend workspace, and open the included examples.
start.workspace.title: Create a clean workspace
start.workspace.lead: Run these steps in the same terminal. Keep the template inventory local to this workspace; an existing project is not required.
start.workspace.expected: A new workspace with its own template inventory. No global CLI installation.
start.install.title: Install the two templates
start.install.lead: Both templates come from the same pinned source revision, {templatesRepository} at {templatesRefShort}. The CLI downloads them into the inventory.
start.install.expected: The CLI reports that frontx-template-shell and frontx-template-mfe are installed.
start.assemble.title: Assemble Shell + MFE
start.assemble.lead: Seed the host first, then add the microfrontend workspace. These commands use the full template identities, not their directory names.
start.assemble.expected: The project appears in my-app. Its .frontx directory records both applied templates.
start.run.title: Run the included examples
start.run.lead: Install the combined workspace, then start the host and its example microfrontends. Keep this terminal running.
start.run.expected: Open http://localhost:5173. Example screens should appear in the host menu.
start.limits.registry: npm install takes the FrontX packages the templates pin from the npm registry.
start.limits.audit: npm install reports audit findings in the templates' dependencies (26 on the tested run).
start.limits.bare: The bare address http://localhost:5173/ shows an empty content area until you choose a screen in the menu.
change.title: Make your first change.
change.lead: Change the title of Blank Home and see it inside your running Shell.
change.before.title: Continue from the quickstart
change.before.text: Complete Run Shell + MFE first. Use the existing my-app folder, with dependencies installed. Stop its running dev:all process with Ctrl+C and stay in the project root, the folder containing package.json.
change.agent.title: First-change agent task
change.find.title: Find the screen
change.find.lead: Blank Home belongs to _blank-mfe. You are changing an included example, not creating a new microfrontend. Keep the application host in src-app/app unchanged.
change.edit.title: Change the English text
change.edit.lead: Open src-app/mfe_packages/_blank-mfe/src/screens/home/i18n/en.json. Change title and description; keep the other five keys. The complete file for this pinned example is shown below. If you have already customized it, edit only those two values.
change.edit.expected: The screen title becomes Project overview. The menu entry remains Blank Home.
change.check.title: Check and restart
change.check.lead: Run from the my-app project root. The first command checks the workspace's TypeScript; dev:all rebuilds the microfrontends, parses their JSON and starts the previews.
change.check.expected: Keep the terminal running. Restart dev:all after changes inside mfe_packages, including translation JSON: these microfrontends are built previews, not hot-reloaded screens.
change.open.title: Open Blank Home
change.open.lead: Open http://localhost:5173 and choose Blank Home. With the host language set to English, the screen should show the title and description below. Other language files are unchanged.
limits.templates: template-shell {shellVersion} and template-mfe {mfeVersion} from {templatesRepository} at commit {templatesRefShort}.
limits.toolchain: Tested with Node {nodeVersion} and npm {npmVersion} on macOS.
overview.panel.templates.title: Understand the templates
overview.panel.templates.text: Browse selected source files and open the screens built from each template before installing.
overview.panel.agent.title: Work with an agent
overview.panel.agent.text: Use a focused task with the first-change guide. AI Kit setup is documented separately.
start.path.new.title: Start a new app
start.path.new.text: Run Shell + MFE, then change your first screen.
start.path.existing.title: Use in an existing app
start.path.existing.text: Choose a library without adopting the full structure.
start.limits.add: frontx add <template> <targetDir> applies a template onto a project you already have; step 3 uses it to add the MFE workspace to my-app.
start.other.title: Other ways to use FrontX
start.other.library.title: Use a library
start.other.library.text: Add individual capabilities to your existing application. UI Kit works independently of the full project structure.
start.other.agent.title: Build with an agent
start.other.agent.text: Set up FrontX AI Kit through Constructor Studio CLI using the upstream guide.
start.band.title: Make it yours
start.band.text: Change the existing Blank Home screen, rebuild it, and see your first edit inside the Shell.
start.run.note.title: Choose Hello World in the menu
start.run.note.text: You should see “Hello World from MFE”. Choose Blank Home to load a different module. The examples flag is intentional: without it, template examples stay hidden and the empty menu is expected.
start.run.note.ports: Uses localhost ports 5173, 3001, 3099, 3201 and 3202. Leave them free; stop the servers with Ctrl+C.
start.limits.requirements: Requires Node 24.14 or later, npm 10 or later, git and a POSIX shell; nothing is installed globally.
change.agent.lead: Use this in the existing project from the quickstart.
change.agent.line1: Continue in the Shell + MFE project created by the FrontX quickstart (my-app).
change.agent.line3: Rename the English Blank Home screen title to "Project overview" and its description to "Your first change is running inside the Shell." Edit only src-app/mfe_packages/_blank-mfe/src/screens/home/i18n/en.json.
change.agent.line4: Keep the Blank Home menu entry, the application shell, shared components and all other translations unchanged. Use the pinned versions from the guides. If the project or prerequisites are missing, explain what is needed before changing anything; do not seed over an existing project.
change.agent.line5: Run npm run type-check --workspace=@gears-frontx/blank-mfe and restart dev:all. Report the changed files and the command results. Do not claim the screen works until it has been opened and checked.
change.find.screen: Screen layout, UI Kit components and bridge subscriptions.
change.find.strings: English text for this screen. This is the file you will edit.
change.find.manifest: Module registration and the Blank Home menu entry. Leave it unchanged.

change.open.screenText: Your first change is running inside the Shell.
change.trouble.title: If something looks different
change.trouble.menu.summary: The menu has no example screens
change.trouble.menu.text: Stop the development servers and restart with FRONTX_INCLUDE_TEMPLATE_EXAMPLES=1 npm run dev:all. The templates deliberately hide their example entries without this flag.
change.trouble.title.summary: The old title is still visible
change.trouble.title.text: Check that you changed _blank-mfe/src/screens/home/i18n/en.json, that the host language is English, and that you restarted dev:all after saving. Then reload the browser. Editing the translation changes the page title, not the Blank Home menu label, which is presentation.label in the package's mfe.json.
change.trouble.workspace.summary: The workspace or a port cannot be found
change.trouble.workspace.text: Run from my-app, not from the outer frontx-start folder or the template inventory. Complete npm install from the quickstart. The examples use ports 5173, 3001, 3099, 3201 and 3202; stop a previous run before restarting.
change.track.title: Keep track of your changes
change.track.lead: .frontx/provenance.json records which templates and source versions were applied. It does not prove that your local edits will merge automatically. Keep a recoverable copy of your work and review changes before any upgrade. Do not rerun seed or add to refresh this screen; the MFE template is applied once per project.
